schema: ai-usage-ledger v1 (DR-1347, DR-1330 D8) — one entry per delivered task: the model that did it, the tokens and dollars where a meter exists, the wall clock measured from the previous push to this push, and an engineer's ESTIMATE of the same work without AI, labelled as an estimate. The slide's project-results table, kept by the build: scripts/ai-usage-ledger.mjs --check fails when a decision record lands without its line. Numbers here are never typed from memory: wallClockHours come from git commit timestamps; sessionTokensObserved is the harness's own budget counter, read, not guessed; tokens per task are null where no meter exposes them, and that is said rather than filled.

sessions.note: Harness budget counter, read at the D7 push. It counts the session's context budget consumed, not a bill; the bill for this session is not metered anywhere this ledger can read, and that is the open item the record names.

entries.task: Lesson sov69: at his day, or at evening - the latency requirement is in the Word as law, and our own watchman runs on the wrong mechanism
entries.notes: Measured from main's previous push (3bae4cac1, pm14, 22:16:10Z) to this lesson's commit (22:44:55Z) = 0.48 h. THAT NUMBER SUBSTANTIALLY UNDERSTATES THE REAL WORK and the reason is on the record rather than smoothed over: everything before the first commit is not in it - reading the 8,924-character send, the duplicate scan across every course and class module, the 38-reference census over app/src and docs/decisions, three refused attempts at the maintainers' primary documentation, the repo-wide systemic measurement of 96 workflows and 6 NAS loops, four passes to settle the reading ladder, a hand rewrite of the senior band after a scripted substitution damaged it, and TWO container restarts that stopped the run mid-build. No per-task tokens or price are exposed by this harness, so tokens and cost stay null rather than being filled with a guess. Estimate is this session's own, for a 69th course lesson carrying five reader versions (child 1584, youth 2290, teen 2356, senior 2814, adult 2967 prose words), two authored parables, 38 references fetched verbatim from the KJV corpus and pinned in 39 spans, a 35-case gate proven to catch, a decision record, a session note, a trust-but-verify audit whose three primary roads were all refused, and a systemic architecture finding traced to named files.
